attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Faithfully restates an evaluative characterization of circular financing. Framed as an observation, but it is an interpretive judgment with no measurable content.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats 'propped up' vs 'functioning well' as a contested judgment with no agreed test, and marks it not adjudicable.

evidence.note: NBC News report from Oct 2025 with an analyst making a similar argument. It shows the view is shared and contested, not that it is true.

reviews.rationale: This is an interpretive judgment about market health with no observable test. Analysts agreeing or disagreeing cannot settle whether the market is 'propped up', so the claim is not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post. The 'peak bubble' self-reference is his own, but it is not scored.

semantics.note: A retrospective observation about investor confidence after Oracle's September 2025 deal. The 'particularly after' qualifier is kept.

contract.note: In context Marcus is talking about AI stocks, so reading 'Wall Street' as confidence in the AI trade is the ordinary informed reading. It is not stretched either way. Leaving the 'peak bubble' self-citation unscored is proper.

evidence.note: Reuters, Dec 2025: Oracle's September enthusiasm turned to doubt, the stock erased its Sept 10 gains, and its CDS hit record highs.
Fortune, Feb 3 2026: Oracle had lost more than half its value since its September high, and investors were questioning its OpenAI exposure.
BofA survey, Nov 2025: a record share of managers said companies were overinvesting, tied to AI capex financing, and 'AI bubble' was the top tail risk.
Nvidia's $5T record in late Oct 2025 shows AI-trade confidence did not drop right after the Oracle deal. Weak counterevidence on timing only.
Overall investor sentiment was high in Nov 2025. That is a whole-market measure, not the AI-trade reading in the contract.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair AI-trade reading, Oracle gave back its September gains and then more than halved, its credit risk spiked, and fund managers flagged AI overinvestment. Nvidia's October record and high broad sentiment are mid-period or off-scope and do not outweigh this.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of Nvidia's price action in his post.

semantics.note: The factual core is the Aug 2025 to Feb 2026 plateau with no crash. 'Run out of gas' could imply the stall would continue, but it is stated in the present tense.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a description of the six-month stall up to the post is ordinary and fits the sentence's tense and its stated prices. Any forward implication is left unscored, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: Barron's, Aug 8 2025: Nvidia closed at a record on Aug 7. The derived close of about $180.7 matches 'about 181'.
Barron's, Feb 4 2026: Nvidia at about $177.55 in early trading, slightly below the Aug 7 level, with no crash.
Nvidia's $5T record in Oct 2025 shows the period was a round trip, not a flat line. The end-to-end result is unchanged.

reviews.rationale: Nvidia went from about $180.7 on Aug 7 2025 to about $177.55 on Feb 4 2026: no net gain and no crash, which meets the support condition. The October peak makes 'plateau' loose but does not contradict it. Later prices are outside the target period.
